option_relations.rationale: Recurrent postpartum mastitis and lactotroph hyperplasia are components of the broader diagnosis of Lymphocytic hypophysitis (postpartum) with hyperprolactinemia and galactorrhea-amenorrhea, complicated by right puerperal mastitis due to Streptococcus agalactiae. The option describes specific aspects of the overall diagnosis.

Hyperprolactinemia is explicitly mentioned as a component of the leaf diagnosis 'Lymphocytic hypophysitis (postpartum) with hyperprolactinemia and galactorrhea-amenorrhea, complicated by right puerperal mastitis due to Streptococcus agalactiae'.
The vignette explicitly states 'No abscess or focal lesion in the right breast' based on ultrasound findings, making subclinical breast abscess unlikely and unrelated to the provided leaf diagnosis.

Bacterial mastitis due to Streptococcus agalactiae is a specific complication mentioned within the broader leaf diagnosis 'Lymphocytic hypophysitis (postpartum) with hyperprolactinemia and galactorrhea-amenorrhea, complicated by right puerperal mastitis due to Streptococcus agalactiae'.
